interpretation: Exact points that re-record Thalassia after a one-year loss are substantially more likely to be unrecorded again the following year than points with uninterrupted occupancy, after stable-node and return-year adjustment. Re-recording therefore marks a comparatively fragile state rather than complete recovery at this annual resolution.
ecological_boundary: The fragility pattern is consistent with hysteresis or incomplete local recovery but can also arise from patchiness, detectability, residual stress, or demographic instability; it does not identify the mechanism.
claim_boundary: Recorded re-loss is an observation-state transition, not mortality or demographic relapse.
Do not treat a one-year Thalassia re-recording as full ecological recovery.
Continuous controls are observational and adjusted for stable node and return year, not experimentally matched.
The result does not identify whether fragility arises from residual rhizomes, local stress, patchiness, detectability, or demographic state.
